newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia c.bank warns against '97 fiscal expansion.
newsitem.headline: Croatia c.bank warns against '97 fiscal expansion.

text.p: Croatia's central bank said on Thursday it was concerned the country's almost 40 billion kuna 1997 government expenditure budget and widening external debt could pose a threat to overall economic stability.
"The bank's council (board) expressed concern over...what it believes is expansionary fiscal policy and additional borrowing," governor Marko Skreb told a news conference.
Skreb described the planned spending as "very large" and warned against possible "undesiderable developments" that could undermine previous efforts to stabilise prices and the exchange rate.
The 1997 budget was raised by over 12 percent from last year's to meet higher public expenditures and repayment of just under 4.0 billion kuna in matured foreign debt.
The parliament, or Sabor, passed the 1997 budget in December, including spending of 39.7 billion kuna and revenue of 36.9 billion.
Although revenues were also projected to rise, they left a sizeable gap that will have to be covered by new borrowing at home and abroad.

But the government vowed the budget deficit target of under 3.0 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP), forecast at 108 billion kuna this year, would not be put in jeopardy. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
